items.title: The canonical one-form and the two-form of a potential presentation: $\lambda=p\cdot dx$ on the Cartesian momentum phase chart and the induced forms on each generalized-coordinate chart
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data and conventions of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]: masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$ and nonempty open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$,
a $C^{2}$ potential $U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ of dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing regularity
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]). Dimensions are read by
[[def-cm01-units]], the Euclidean product on $\mathbb R^{3N}$ is
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. Write $n:=3N\ge1$. The
Cartesian momentum phase chart of the presentation is
$I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ with the momentum $p=\mathsf Mv$ of
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]], and the momentum phase chart of a
generalized-coordinate map $X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r$ coordinates is
$I_{0}\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ with the generalized momentum
$P=G(q)v$, $G(q)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q)$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-hyperregularity]]).

**(a) Cartesian chart.** The **Cartesian phase domain of the presentation** is
the nonempty open set

$$W:=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n},\qquad z=(x,p),$$

a phase domain in the sense of [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]]
(openness is clause (a) of [[def-cm01-configuration]]; nonemptiness is an
explicit hypothesis here, so an empty configuration domain has no instances
of this phase-domain definition). On $W$ the
**canonical one-form of the presentation in the Cartesian chart** is the smooth
one-form

$$\lambda_{(x,p)}(\delta x,\delta p):=p\cdot\delta x\qquad\bigl((x,p)\in W,\ (\delta x,\delta p)\in\mathbb R^{3N}\times\mathbb R^{3N}\bigr),$$

where $p\cdot\delta x$ is the Euclidean pairing of the momentum covector with
the displacement, and the **two-form of the presentation in the Cartesian
chart** is

$$\omega:=-d\lambda$$

([[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]). In coordinates, reading
$x=(x^{1},\dots,x^{3N})$ and $p=(p_{1},\dots,p_{3N})$ as the standard
coordinates of $W$,

$$\lambda=\sum_{a=1}^{3N}p_{a}\,dx^{a},\qquad \omega=\sum_{a=1}^{3N}dx^{a}\wedge dp_{a},\qquad \omega_{(x,p)}\bigl((\delta x,\delta p),(\delta x',\delta p')\bigr)=\delta x\cdot\delta p'-\delta p\cdot\delta x',$$

the last identity using the Euclidean product. The dimension of both forms is
that of action, $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$: the pairing of a momentum
($\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$) with a displacement ($\ell$). The forms have no
explicit time dependence; for each $t\in I_{0}$ the slice $\{t\}\times W$
carries the same two-form. The momentum phase chart with time,
$I_{0}\times W$ with coordinates $(t,x,p)$, is the domain of the Hamiltonians
and fields of this page. The **sign convention** fixed by
[[def-hamiltonian-vector-field-and-hamiltonian-function]] and used
throughout is $\iota_{X}\omega=dH$; $H$ denotes a phase function as in that
item.

**(b) Generalized-coordinate chart.** Let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be a
generalized-coordinate map with substituted Lagrangian $\widetilde L$ and
kinetic metric $G$, and let $r$ be its number of coordinates
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]). The **chart map of the
presentation in the coordinates $X$** is

$$\Phi_{X}:\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}\longrightarrow Q\times\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad \Phi_{X}(q,P):=\Bigl(X(q),\ \mathsf M\,DX(q)\,G(q)^{-1}P\Bigr).$$

Here $DX(q)$ is the $(3N)\times r$ Jacobian of $X$ at $q$
([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]), $G(q)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q)$
is symmetric positive definite ([[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]],
[[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]), and $P$ is a
generalized momentum. The image of $\Phi_{X}$ is

$$\Phi_{X}(\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r})=\bigl\{\,(X(q),\mathsf M\,DX(q)v)\ :\ q\in\Omega,\ v\in\mathbb R^{r}\,\bigr\},$$

the momentum chart of the presentation in the coordinates $X$; indeed
$P\mapsto v=G(q)^{-1}P$ is a linear bijection of $\mathbb R^{r}$. The map
$\Phi_X$ is $C^2$: $X$ is $C^3$, so $DX$ is $C^2$; hence
$G=DX^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M DX$ is $C^2$, and $G^{-1}$ is $C^2$ because
matrix inversion is given by the adjugate divided by the nonvanishing
determinant on the positive-definite matrices. The fiber
coefficient $\mathsf M DX(q)G(q)^{-1}$ is $C^2$. Thus $\Phi_X$ is a
$C^2$ immersion:
its derivative is injective at every point, because $DX(q)$ is injective
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-euclidean-submersions-and-immersions]]) and $P\mapsto G(q)^{-1}P$ is a
linear bijection; when $r=3N$ its derivative is invertible and it is a local
$C^2$ diffeomorphism onto its open image in $W$
(equivalently $\mathsf M\,DX(q)G(q)^{-1}=DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}$: see the
recorded identity below). We use the pointwise coordinate pullback: for a smooth
$k$-form $\eta$ on $W$, set
$(\Phi_X^*\eta)_{(q,P)}(v_1,\dots,v_k):=
\eta_{\Phi_X(q,P)}(D\Phi_X(q,P)v_1,\dots,D\Phi_X(q,P)v_k)$, extending the
formula of [[def-pullback-of-a-differential-form]] to this $C^2$ map. The
result has continuous coefficients. The **forms of the presentation in the
coordinates $X$** are

$$\lambda_{X}:=\Phi_{X}^{*}\lambda,\qquad \omega_{X}:=\Phi_{X}^{*}\omega$$

([[def-pullback-of-a-differential-form]]). In the coordinates $(q,P)$ on
$\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ the following identities hold, and are proved in
clause 2 of the symplectic-structure theorem of this page:

$$\lambda_{X}=\sum_{a=1}^{r}P_{a}\,dq^{a},\qquad \omega_{X}=\sum_{a=1}^{r}dq^{a}\wedge dP_{a};$$

moreover, when $r=3N$ and $DX(q)$ is invertible,
$\mathsf M\,DX(q)G(q)^{-1}=DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}$, so that on an open
generalized-coordinate chart the chart map reads
$\Phi_X(q,P)=\bigl(X(q),DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}P\bigr)$ and the chart transition
between the two descriptions of the same momentum datum is a $C^2$ local
diffeomorphism.

**(c) Status.** The item defines the two-form datum of the declared
presentation on its declared charts, together with the sign convention for
fields. It asserts no closedness, no nondegeneracy, no equation of motion, no
conservation law and no measured value; those are the subject of the other
items of this page. The forms depend on the declared chart and its coordinate
dimensions, but not on the residual forces $d$ nor on the normalization
$U\mapsto U+c(t)$ of the potential representative. All objects are model
objects of the idealization declared by the force branch.
items.physical_scope: The symplectic data of a potential presentation of the framework's force branch: on the Cartesian momentum phase chart $Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ the canonical one-form $\lambda=p\cdot\delta x$ and the two-form $\omega=-d\lambda$, and on each declared generalized-coordinate momentum chart the forms pulled back along the presentation's own chart map $(q,P)\mapsto(X(q),\mathsf M\,DX(q)G(q)^{-1}P)$. The item defines model objects of the declared presentation and its declared chart only; it asserts no closedness, nondegeneracy, dynamics or measured value, and it fixes the sign convention $\iota_X\omega=dH$ used throughout this page.

items.title: The two-form of a potential presentation is closed and nondegenerate, and each generalized-coordinate momentum chart carries the same symplectic structure: $\Phi_X^*\lambda=\sum P_a\,dq^a$ and $\Phi_X^*\omega=\sum dq^a\wedge dP_a$
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data, charts and forms of [[def-cm13-two-form]]: masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$,
open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ and mass operator
$\mathsf M$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]), time window $I_{0}$, $C^{2}$
potential $U$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing regularity
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-units]]), the Cartesian phase
domain $W=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ with $n=3N$, its canonical one-form
$\lambda$ and two-form $\omega=-d\lambda$, and for each generalized-coordinate
map $X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r$ coordinates and kinetic metric $G$ the chart map
$\Phi_{X}(q,P)=(X(q),\mathsf M\,DX(q)G(q)^{-1}P)$ with pullbacks
$\lambda_{X}=\Phi_{X}^{*}\lambda$ and $\omega_{X}=\Phi_{X}^{*}\omega$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]], [[def-cm12-hyperregularity]]). Then:

1. **(Cartesian chart)** $\omega$ is the standard two-form of the phase
   domain $W$ in the sense of
   [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]]: $d\omega=0$ and
   $\omega$ is nondegenerate at every point of $W$; hence $(W,\omega)$ is a
   symplectic manifold in the sense of
   [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]].
2. **(generalized-coordinate chart)** On $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$,

$$\lambda_{X}=\sum_{a=1}^{r}P_{a}\,dq^{a},\qquad \omega_{X}=\sum_{a=1}^{r}dq^{a}\wedge dP_{a};$$

   consequently $\omega_{X}$ is closed and nondegenerate at every point, so
   $\Phi_{X}^{*}\omega$ is the standard two-form of the phase domain
   $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ and $\Phi_{X}$ preserves the two-form.
3. **(full-dimensional chart transitions)** Let $X_1,X_2$ be generalized-coordinate
   charts with $r=3N$, and restrict their momentum chart maps to neighborhoods
   on which each $\Phi_{X_j}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of the
   Cartesian phase domain. On every overlap of those image neighborhoods,
   the genuine phase-chart transition
   $\Theta=\Phi_{X_2}^{-1}\circ\Phi_{X_1}$ preserves the two-form. The
   difference $\lambda_{X_1}-\Theta^*\lambda_{X_2}$ is a closed one-form
   there; no exactness is asserted. Lower-dimensional generalized-coordinate
   immersions have the symplectic pullback form of clause 2, but are not
   transitions between open full-dimensional phase charts.

The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the
declared presentation and the cited mathematics. It asserts no equation of
motion, no conservation law, no completeness of any flow and no empirical
content.
items.physical_scope: The symplectic structure of a declared potential presentation of the force branch: on the Cartesian momentum phase chart the two-form $\omega=\sum dx^a\wedge dp_a$ is closed and nondegenerate, and on each declared generalized-coordinate momentum chart the pullback of the presentation's two-form along the presentation's own chart map has the canonical coordinate expression. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no dynamics, no conservation law and no measured value.

items.title: Canonical coordinates and the canonical form of the two-form for a potential presentation: the coordinate expression $\omega=\sum_{a=1}^{m} d\theta^a\wedge d\theta^{m+a}$ with $m$ the chart's half-dimension, and the model's own momentum charts
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
momentum charts, the phase domains and the two-form datum of
[[def-cm13-two-form]]: the Cartesian phase domain $W=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$
with $n=3N$, its two-form $\omega$, and for each generalized-coordinate map
$X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r$ coordinates the chart map $\Phi_{X}$ and the form
$\omega_{X}$ ([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]], [[def-cm01-configuration]]). All
differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) Canonical coordinates.** Let $W_{0}\subseteq W$ (or
$W_{0}\subseteq\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$) be nonempty open, and let

$$\theta=(\theta^{1},\dots,\theta^{2m}):W_{0}\longrightarrow V\subseteq\mathbb R^{2m}$$

be a $C^{1}$ chart of $W_{0}$ onto an open set $V$ ([[def-metric-topology]]),
with $m$ the half-dimension of $W_{0}$. Write $\sigma=\omega|_{W_0}$ and $\alpha=\lambda|_{W_0}$ in the Cartesian case, and $\sigma=\omega_X|_{W_0}$ and $\alpha=\lambda_X|_{W_0}$ in the generalized-coordinate case. Each coordinate $\theta^a$ has a declared dimension $\eta_a$ and unit; its paired coordinate $\theta^{m+a}$ has dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1}\eta_a^{-1}$ and a declared compatible unit, so every summand below has action dimension. Coordinate formulas use the numerical representatives in these fixed units. The coordinates $\theta$ are
**canonical coordinates for the presentation's two-form** on $W_{0}$ when the
two-form takes the **canonical form**

$$\sigma=\sum_{a=1}^{m}d\theta^{a}\wedge d\theta^{m+a}$$

pointwise on $W_{0}$, using the finite-coordinate form and pullback conventions of [[def-cm-finite-regularity-canonical-calculus]]; equivalently, when the
pullback identity $\theta^{*}\omega_{V}^{\mathrm{st}}=\sigma$ holds
for the standard two-form $\omega_{V}^{\mathrm{st}}$ of $V$
([[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]],
[[def-cm-finite-regularity-canonical-calculus]]), equivalently when
$D\theta(z)^{\mathsf T}J\,D\theta(z)=J$ for the standard symplectic matrix
$J$ at every $z\in W_{0}$
([[prop-cm-canonical-map-tests-and-hamiltonian-transport]]). A **canonical
chart of the presentation** is a chart whose coordinates are canonical in
this sense; the equivalence with the canonical maps defined later on this
page is recorded with those definitions.

**(b) The model's own charts are canonical.** The Cartesian coordinates
$(x,p)$ on $W$ are canonical coordinates: by clause 1 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] the two-form is
$\omega=\sum_{a}dx^{a}\wedge dp_{a}$. For a generalized-coordinate map, the
coordinates $(q,P)$ on $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ are canonical coordinates
for the pulled-back form $\omega_{X}$: by clause 2 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] one has
$\omega_{X}=\sum_{a}dq^{a}\wedge dP_{a}$, and when the map is a genuine chart
($r=3N$) the chart transition is a change of canonical coordinates on
overlaps.

**(c) Canonical one-form up to gauge at classical differentiability.** For a $C^2$ canonical chart $\theta$, the source canonical one-form $\alpha$ specified in clause (a) from
[[def-cm13-two-form]] is said to be **in canonical form up to gauge** in the
canonical coordinates $\theta$ when the difference
$\alpha-\sum_{a}\theta^{m+a}d\theta^{a}$ is a closed one-form on $W_{0}$;
exactness of that difference is not required. For the presentation's own
charts the difference of the two canonical one-forms is closed by clause 3 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]]. These charts are $C^2$ or smoother. For a merely $C^1$ chart clause (a) retains its full pointwise meaning, but the coefficients of the pulled-back one-form may be only continuous, so this clause does not apply the classical exterior derivative to them.

**(d) Status and warnings.** The item defines a coordinate condition on a
declared chart and records the one fact that the presentation's own momentum
charts satisfy it. It asserts no existence of canonical coordinates beyond
the model's charts, no global statement on multiply connected phase domains,
no dynamics and no measured value. A chart that is merely a diffeomorphism
need not be canonical; the determinant test
$|\det D\theta|=1$ is necessary but, in dimension $2m\ge4$, not sufficient
for canonicity (the scope remark of this page records the witness).
items.physical_scope: The vocabulary of canonical coordinates for the two-form of a declared potential presentation: coordinates on a phase domain in which the presentation's two-form takes the canonical coordinate expression, and the record that the presentation's Cartesian momentum chart and each of its generalized-coordinate momentum charts are canonical charts. The item defines a coordinate condition and fixes the vocabulary used by the bracket, field, flow and generating-function items; it asserts no dynamics, no existence of canonical coordinates beyond the model's own charts and no measured value.

items.title: The Hamiltonian field of a phase function for a potential presentation: the unique field $X_f$ with $\iota_{X_f}\omega=df$, and $X_H=(H_p,-H_x)$ for the branch Hamiltonian
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]] and the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]]: the Cartesian phase domain
$W=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$, its two-form $\omega$, a generalized-coordinate
chart map $\Phi_{X}$ and the form $\omega_{X}$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]); the presentation is
hyperregular on every chart with the Hamiltonian $H$ of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]] and [[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]],

$$H(t,x,p)=\tfrac12\,p\cdot\mathsf M^{-1}p+U(t,x),\qquad \widetilde H(t,q,P)=\tfrac12\,P\cdot G(q)^{-1}P+\widetilde U(t,q).$$

Differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], and gradients those of
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]].

**(a) The field of a phase function.** Let $W_{0}\subseteq W$ be nonempty
open and let $f:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{2}$. By clause 1 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] the form $\omega$ is nondegenerate on
$W_{0}$, so there is exactly one $C^{1}$ vector field $X_{f}$ on $W_{0}$ with

$$\iota_{X_{f}}\omega=df$$

(the sign convention of [[def-hamiltonian-vector-field-and-hamiltonian-function]]
and [[prop-cm-hamiltonian-field-and-poisson-bracket-in-a-phase-chart]]); it
is the **Hamiltonian field of $f$ for the presentation**. In the Cartesian
coordinates $(x,p)$, writing $\nabla f=(f_{x^{1}},\dots,f_{x^{3N}},f_{p_{1}},\dots,f_{p_{3N}})$,

$$X_{f}=\bigl(f_{p},\,-f_{x}\bigr)=J\nabla f,\qquad J=\begin{pmatrix}0_{3N}&I_{3N}\\-I_{3N}&0_{3N}\end{pmatrix};$$

in any canonical chart $(\theta^{1},\dots,\theta^{2m})$ of the presentation
the same field reads $X_{f}=\bigl(f_{\theta^{m+1}},\dots,f_{\theta^{2m}},-f_{\theta^{1}},\dots,-f_{\theta^{m}}\bigr)$.
A vector field on $W_{0}$ is called **Hamiltonian for the presentation** when
it is $X_{f}$ for some $C^{2}$ function $f$; in particular
$X_{f}=0$ exactly when $f$ is locally constant on $W_{0}$. Vector fields are
read as tangent-bundle sections of
[[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]].

**(b) The field of the branch Hamiltonian.** For each $t\in I_{0}$ the
function $H_{t}:=H(t,\cdot)$ is $C^{2}$ on $W$, and the **Hamiltonian field
of the presentation** at time $t$ is $X_{H_{t}}$:

$$X_{H_{t}}(x,p)=\bigl(\mathsf M^{-1}p,\ -\nabla_{x}U(t,x)\bigr),$$

whose components are a velocity and a force. In the coordinates $X$ the
corresponding field is
$X_{\widetilde H_{t}}(q,P)=\bigl(G(q)^{-1}P,\ -\partial_{q}\widetilde H(t,q,P)\bigr)$,
where the second slot retains the kinetic contribution
$-\tfrac12P\cdot\partial_{q}(G(q)^{-1})P$ when the metric varies. If
$d\not\equiv0$ the model's forced evolution carries the additional momentum
source $d$; the corresponding vector field
$(x,p)\mapsto\bigl(\mathsf M^{-1}p,-\nabla_{x}U(t,x)+d(t,x,\mathsf M^{-1}p)\bigr)$
is generally not a Hamiltonian field for the presentation, and it is one
exactly when the residual force has a potential independent of the velocity
slot (the criterion is proved in clause 4 of the corresponding theorem of this
page).

**(c) Time dependence and status.** For a time-dependent $H$ the assignment
$t\mapsto X_{H_{t}}$ is a time-dependent field on the phase domain; each
$X_{H_{t}}$ is $C^{1}$, hence locally Lipschitz in the state variable, and no
completeness of its integral curves is asserted here. The item defines the
field datum and its chart expressions; the identification of the model's
motions with the integral curves, and all conservation or invariance
properties, are the subject of the other items of this page. The field is
defined by the intrinsic equation $\iota_{X}\omega=dH$ and therefore does not
depend on the canonical chart used to compute it.
items.physical_scope: The Hamiltonian field datum of a declared potential presentation: for a $C^{2}$ phase function the unique $C^{1}$ field contracted against the presentation's two-form to the differential, together with its coordinate expression in the model's Cartesian and generalized-coordinate charts and its specialization to the branch Hamiltonian, including the residual-force source that is generally not a Hamiltonian field. The item defines model fields and their chart expressions; it asserts no existence of integral curves, no equation of motion and no measured value.

items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data, charts and Hamiltonian field of [[def-cm13-two-form]],
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]]: masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$ and open
configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ with mass operator
$\mathsf M$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]), time window $I_{0}$, $C^{2}$
potential $U$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing regularity
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-units]]), the Cartesian
Hamiltonian $H(t,x,p)=	frac12p\cdot\mathsf M^{-1}p+U(t,x)$ and, for a
generalized-coordinate map $X:\Omega	o Q$ with kinetic metric
$G=DX^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX$, the chart Hamiltonian
$\widetilde H(t,q,P)=	frac12P\cdot G(q)^{-1}P+\widetilde U(t,q)$
([[def-cm12-hamiltonian]], [[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]],
[[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]). Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be a nonempty open
interval. For clause 4, a time-dependent phase function is a map
$f:I_{0}	imes W	o\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$; write $f_{t}(z):=f(t,z)$
and use [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]] to define the associated family of
Hamiltonian fields $t\mapsto X_{f_t}$. The forced field is called Hamiltonian
on this full chart when it equals $X_{f_t}$ for every $t\in I_{0}$. Then:

1. **(potential branch, Cartesian chart)** Assume $d\equiv0$ on the state
   domain. For a $C^{2}$ curve $x:J	o Q$ with $p(t):=\mathsf Mx'(t)$ the
   following are equivalent: (a) $x$ is a motion of the model
   ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]); (b) $\dot x(t)=H_{p}(t,x(t),p(t))$ and
   $\dot p(t)=-H_{x}(t,x(t),p(t))$ for every $t\in J$; (c) the curve
   $t\mapsto(x(t),p(t))$ is an integral curve of the time-dependent field
   $t\mapsto X_{H_{t}}$, i.e. satisfies
   $\dot z(t)=X_{H_{t}}(z(t))$ with $z=(x,p)$
   ([[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]).
2. **(generalized-coordinate chart)** Let $X:\Omega	o Q$ be a
   generalized-coordinate map and let $q:J	o\Omega$ be a $C^{2}$ curve with
   $x:=X\circ q$ and $P(t):=G(q(t))q'(t)$. Then the declared Lagrange
   equations with residual generalized force,
   $\Lambda(\widetilde L)(q)(t)=Q^{\mathrm{res}}(t,q(t),q'(t))$, are
   equivalent to
   $q'(t)=\widetilde H_{P}(t,q(t),P(t))$ and
   $P'(t)=-\widetilde H_{q}(t,q(t),P(t))+Q^{\mathrm{res}}(t,q(t),q'(t))$;
   in particular, when $d\equiv0$, they are equivalent to
   $(q,P)$ being an integral curve of $X_{\widetilde H_{t}}$.
3. **(residual forces, Cartesian chart)** For a $C^{2}$ curve $x:J	o Q$
   with $p=\mathsf Mx'$, the model's forced equation
   $\mathsf Mx''=-
abla_{x}U(t,x)+d(t,x,x')$ holds on $J$ if and only if
   $\dot x=H_{p}$ and $\dot p=-H_{x}+d(t,x,\mathsf M^{-1}p)$ on $J$.
4. **(when is the forced field Hamiltonian?)** The forced field
   $(x,p)\mapsto igl(\mathsf M^{-1}p,-
abla_{x}U(t,x)+d(t,x,\mathsf M^{-1}p) igr)$
   is Hamiltonian in the preceding time-dependent sense if and only if there
   is a $C^{2}$ function $V:I_{0}	imes Q	o\mathbb R$ with
   $d(t,x,v)=-
abla_{x}V(t,x)$ for every $(t,x,v)$ of the state domain; in
   that case the phase function is $H+V$ up to an independently chosen
   additive $C^2$ function of $t$ on each connected component of $Q$, and the model's forced motions are the motions of the potential
   presentation $(U+V,0)$.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation and the declared chart; it asserts no existence or uniqueness of
solutions, no completeness, no conservation law and no empirical content.

items.title: The Poisson bracket of phase functions of a potential presentation: $\{f,g\}=\omega(X_f,X_g)$ and the coordinate formula in each canonical chart
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]] and the Hamiltonian fields of
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]]. Dimensions are read by [[def-cm01-units]];
differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) Phase functions.** Let $W_{0}$ be a nonempty open subset of a phase
domain of the presentation. A **phase function of the presentation on
$W_{0}$ of class $C^{k}$** is a map $f:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{k}$
($k\ge1$); its physical reading is a model quantity computed from the
positions and momenta of the labels, and its dimension is declared as part of
the datum. A **time-dependent phase function** on an interval $J\subseteq
I_{0}$ is a map $f:J\times W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ of the declared class, written
$f_{t}:=f(t,\cdot)$.

**(b) The bracket.** For $C^1$ phase functions $f,g:W_0\to\mathbb R$, define their **Poisson bracket for the presentation** by the pointwise coordinate formula $\{f,g\}=\nabla f^{\mathsf T}J\nabla g$ in a canonical chart, in the finite-regularity convention of [[def-cm-finite-regularity-canonical-calculus]]. This is a continuous function. The definition is independent of the canonical chart: for a canonical $C^1$ coordinate change with derivative $M$, the matrix identity implies $MJM^{\mathsf T}=J$, and the equivalence of the two matrix identities is proved in [[prop-cm-canonical-map-tests-and-hamiltonian-transport]], and the chain rule transforms the two gradients so their pairing is unchanged.

When both functions are $C^2$, their Hamiltonian fields of [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]] are $C^1$, and the bracket has the intrinsic formula
$$\{f,g\}=\omega(X_f,X_g)=df(X_g)=X_g(f)=-X_f(g).$$
In this case it is $C^1$, with the same sign convention as the smooth root bracket and [[prop-cm-hamiltonian-field-and-poisson-bracket-in-a-phase-chart]]. The extension to $C^1$ inputs makes evolution identities for $C^1$ observables and nested brackets of $C^2$ functions meaningful; it does not assert closure of the $C^2$ class under the bracket. Its dimension is $[f][g](\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1})^{-1}$, the product of the entries' dimensions divided by the action dimension of the two-form.

**(c) Coordinate formula.** In the Cartesian canonical coordinates $(x,p)$
of the presentation, and more generally in any canonical chart
$(\theta^{1},\dots,\theta^{2m})$ of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]],

$$\{f,g\}=\sum_{a=1}^{3N}\Bigl(f_{x^{a}}g_{p_{a}}-f_{p_{a}}g_{x^{a}}\Bigr)=\nabla f^{\mathsf T}J\,\nabla g,\qquad \{f,g\}=\sum_{a=1}^{m}\Bigl(f_{\theta^{a}}g_{\theta^{m+a}}-f_{\theta^{m+a}}g_{\theta^{a}}\Bigr),$$

with derivatives those of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. The coordinate formula is
recorded here and its identities (bilinearity, skew-symmetry, the Leibniz
rule, the Jacobi identity and the fundamental brackets) are proved in the
bracket-identities theorem of this page.

**(d) Status.** The item defines a bilinear operation on the declared phase
domain by the pointwise coordinate formula, and for $C^2$ entries by $\{f,g\}=\omega(X_f,X_g)$, hence
independently of the canonical chart used to evaluate the coordinate
formula. It asserts no equation of motion, no conservation law, no algebraic
identity beyond well-definedness and no measured value; in particular the
bracket with the Hamiltonian and the notion of first integral are the subject
of the evolution theorem of this page.
items.physical_scope: The pointwise bracket is defined for C1 inputs, with the C2 intrinsic-field expression and C1 output regularity retained. The item defines a model bilinear operation and fixes its dimension; it asserts no algebraic identity, no equation of motion, no conservation law and no measured value.

items.title: The bracket of a potential presentation is bilinear, skew, a derivation in each slot, satisfies the Jacobi identity, and reproduces the fundamental brackets and the Hamiltonian field
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]], the Hamiltonian fields of
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]] and the bracket of [[def-cm13-poisson]] on a
nonempty open subset $W_{0}$ of a phase domain of the presentation. Then:

1. **(bilinearity and skew-symmetry)** The bracket is real-bilinear:
   $\{\alpha f+\beta g,h\}=\alpha\{f,h\}+\beta\{g,h\}$ and
   $\{f,\alpha g+\beta h\}=\alpha\{f,g\}+\beta\{f,h\}$ for real $\alpha,\beta$
   and $C^{2}$ phase functions; it is skew-symmetric,
   $\{f,g\}=-\{g,f\}$, and in particular $\{f,f\}=0$.
2. **(Leibniz rule)** For $C^{2}$ functions $f,g,h$,

$$\{f,gh\}=\{f,g\}h+g\{f,h\},\qquad \{fg,h\}=f\{g,h\}+g\{f,h\}.$$

3. **(Jacobi identity)** For $C^{2}$ functions $f,g,h$,

$$\{f,\{g,h\}\}+\{g,\{h,f\}\}+\{h,\{f,g\}\}=0.$$

4. **(relation to the fields)** For $C^{2}$ functions $f,g$ one has
   $\{f,g\}=X_{g}(f)=-X_{f}(g)=d\!f(X_{g})=-d\!g(X_{f})$, and the bracket is
   $C^{1}$; in the Cartesian canonical coordinates
   $\{f,g\}=\sum_{a}(f_{x^{a}}g_{p_{a}}-f_{p_{a}}g_{x^{a}})=\nabla f^{\mathsf T}J\,\nabla g$,
   and in any canonical chart $(\theta^{1},\dots,\theta^{2m})$ the analogous
   formula of [[def-cm13-poisson]] clause (c) holds.
5. **(fundamental brackets)** In the Cartesian canonical coordinates the
   coordinate functions satisfy $\{x^{a},x^{b}\}=0$, $\{p_{a},p_{b}\}=0$ and
   $\{x^{a},p_{b}\}=\delta^{a}_{b}$; more generally, in any canonical chart
   $(\theta^{1},\dots,\theta^{2m})$ one has
   $\{\theta^{i},\theta^{j}\}=J^{ij}$, the entries of the standard symplectic
   matrix.

For nested brackets use the pointwise $C^1$-slot coordinate extension of [[def-cm-finite-regularity-canonical-calculus]], which agrees with the presentation bracket on $C^2$ inputs. Thus the Jacobi identity above is meaningful for $C^2$ functions despite their brackets being only $C^1$. The $C^2$ class is not in general closed under the bracket and is not asserted to be a Poisson algebra. The smooth $C^\infty$ phase functions, equipped with this bracket and pointwise product, form a Poisson algebra.
The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no equation of motion, no
conservation law and no measured value.

items.title: Evolution of phase functions along the model's Hamiltonian solutions: $df/dt=\partial_t f+\{f,H\}$, the first-integral criterion, and the closed bracket algebra of autonomous first integrals
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the Hamiltonian
fields of [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]], the bracket of
[[def-cm13-poisson]] and the branch Hamiltonian $H$, assumed of class $C^{2}$
in $(t,z)$ on $I_{0}\times W$ ([[def-cm12-hamiltonian]],
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-configuration]],
[[def-cm01-units]]). Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be a nonempty open interval and
let $z:J\to W$ be a $C^{1}$ solution of the Hamiltonian system
$\dot z(t)=X_{H_{t}}(z(t))$, equivalently, when $d\equiv0$ on the state domain and with
$z=(x,p)$ and $p=\mathsf Mx'$, the momentum-phase curve of a motion of the
model ([[pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations]],
[[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]],
[[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]). Then:

1. **(evolution identity)** Let $\mathcal U\subseteq J\times W$ be an open
   neighborhood of the solution graph $\{(t,z(t)):t\in J\}$, and let
   $f:\mathcal U\to\mathbb R$ be $C^{1}$. For
   $\mathcal U_t:=\{w\in W:(t,w)\in\mathcal U\}$ and
   $f_t:=f(t,\cdot)$, the function $t\mapsto f(t,z(t))$ is differentiable on
   $J$ and

$$\frac{d}{dt}f\bigl(t,z(t)\bigr)=\partial_{t}f\bigl(t,z(t)\bigr)+\{f_{t},H_{t}\}\bigl(z(t)\bigr),$$

   where $f_t:=f(t,\cdot)$, $H_t:=H(t,\cdot)$ and the bracket is that of
   [[def-cm13-poisson]], evaluated on the open slice $\mathcal U_t$.
2. **(first integrals)** If $f$ is autonomous and
   $\{f,H_{t}\}(z(t))=0$ for every $t\in J$, then $f\circ z$ is constant on
   $J$; in particular, if in addition $H$ is autonomous
   ($\partial_{t}U\equiv0$ and $d\equiv0$), then $H$ itself is constant
   along $z$, the Hamiltonian form of the energy conservation of
   [[pthm-cm12-energy-time]].
3. **(closed algebra)** Let $H$ be autonomous and let $f,g$ be autonomous
   $C^{3}$ phase functions with $\{f,H\}=0$ and $\{g,H\}=0$ everywhere on
   their common domain. Then $\{f,g\}$ is again a first integral of $H$:
   $\{\{f,g\},H\}=0$ everywhere, and $\{f,g\}$ is constant along every
   solution of the Hamiltonian system on which it is defined.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no empirical content and
no existence, uniqueness or completeness of solutions.
items.physical_scope: The evolution identity of the declared potential presentation: along the model's Hamiltonian solutions the total time derivative of a phase function is its explicit time derivative plus the bracket with the branch Hamiltonian; autonomous functions with vanishing bracket are constant on trajectories, and, for an autonomous Hamiltonian, the bracket of two autonomous $C^{3}$ first integrals is again a first integral and the Hamiltonian itself is a first integral. Identification of Hamiltonian solutions with force-model motions requires $d\equiv0$ on the state domain. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no empirical content.

items.title: Canonical maps of a potential presentation: pullback-preserving immersions and the equal-dimensional determinant and field-transport tests
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]] and the Hamiltonian fields of
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]]
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]). Let $W_j\subseteq\mathbb R^{2m_j}$ be
nonempty open subsets of phase domains of the presentation, carrying their
respective two-forms $\omega_j$ from [[def-cm13-two-form]] (for a
generalized-coordinate domain this is the pulled-back form $\omega_X$ in its
own $(q,P)$ coordinates). The dimensions $2m_1$ and $2m_2$ need not agree.

**(a) Pullback-preserving maps and transformations.** A $C^{1}$ map
$C:W_{1}\to W_{2}$ is a **canonical map of the presentation** when

$$C^{*}\omega_{2}=\omega_{1}\qquad\text{on }W_{1}$$

with pointwise pullback as in [[def-pullback-of-a-differential-form]]. In
standard phase coordinates this is the dimension-aware matrix identity

$$DC(z)^{\mathsf T}J_{m_2}DC(z)=J_{m_1},$$

where $DC(z)$ is a $2m_2\times2m_1$ matrix and
$J_m=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_m\\-I_m&0\end{pmatrix}$. It forces $DC(z)$ to be
injective: if $DC(z)v=0$, then $v^{\mathsf T}J_{m_1}w=0$ for every $w$, so
$v=0$ by nondegeneracy of $J_{m_1}$, so $m_1\le m_2$. Thus it is a $C^1$
immersion preserving the symplectic forms (a symplectic immersion). If it is
also a $C^1$ embedding of the underlying
manifolds (injective and a homeomorphism onto its image), call it a
**canonical embedding**; pullback preservation alone asserts no global
injectivity or topological embedding.

When $m_1=m_2$, a canonical map is automatically a local diffeomorphism by
the inverse function theorem; call it a **local canonical transformation**.
A **canonical transformation** is a canonical map that is a $C^1$
diffeomorphism onto $W_2$. The same-dimensional definitions agree with the
finite-regularity convention of
[[def-cm-finite-regularity-canonical-calculus]]; the $C^\infty$ case agrees
with [[def-canonical-transformation]] and
[[def-symplectomorphism-local-symplectomorphism-and-symplectic-embedding]].
The different-dimensional definition here extends those finite-coordinate
notions only by the displayed pullback equality.

**(b) Equal-dimensional matrix and determinant tests.** If $m_1=m_2=m$,
then by [[prop-cm-canonical-map-tests-and-hamiltonian-transport]] clause 1
the pullback condition is equivalent to

$$DC(z)^{\mathsf T}J_m\,DC(z)=J_m\qquad\text{for every }z\in W_{1}.$$

The derivative is invertible at every point, so the map is a local
diffeomorphism by [[thm-euclidean-inverse-function-theorem]]. Taking
determinants of the matrix identity gives $(\det DC(z))^2=1$, hence
$|\det DC(z)|=1$ for every $z$
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]],
[[cor-square-matrix-invertible-iff-determinant-is-a-unit]],
[[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]]). In dimension $2m\ge4$ the condition
$|\det DC|=1$ alone is strictly weaker than canonicity (the companion page
carries an explicit volume-preserving, non-canonical shear), while for $m=1$ the symplectic condition is exactly $\det DC=1$; absolute determinant $1$ alone also admits orientation-reversing, antisymplectic maps.
If $m_1\ne m_2$, $DC$ is rectangular, so no square determinant test is
defined; the dimension-aware pullback identity of clause (a) is the criterion.

**(c) Elementary closure and equal-dimensional field transport.** By
pointwise functoriality of pullback, the identity map, composites of
composable canonical maps and inverses of canonical transformations are
canonical. For a $C^{2}$ equal-dimensional canonical map
$C:W_{1}\to W_{2}$ and a $C^{2}$ function $f$ on $W_{2}$, the Hamiltonian
fields satisfy

$$DC(z)\,X_{f\circ C}(z)=X_{f}\bigl(C(z)\bigr)\qquad(z\in W_{1}),$$

so that $C$ conjugates the Hamiltonian system of $f\circ C$ to that of $f$
by the chain rule and the equal-dimensional matrix identity: taking the
inverse of $DC^{\mathsf T}J_mDC=J_m$ gives $DCJ_mDC^{\mathsf T}=J_m$, which
substituted into $DCJ_m\nabla(f\circ C)$ yields the displayed identity. No
such ambient field-transport identity is asserted for a lower-dimensional
symplectic immersion: the ambient field need not be tangent to its image.
Bracket, solution and phase-volume consequences are likewise limited to
their stated equal-dimensional local transformations.

**(d) The model's canonical maps.** For every generalized-coordinate
immersion $X$, the momentum map $\Phi_X$ in [[def-cm13-two-form]] is a
dimension-aware canonical map by clause 2 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]]; it is a symplectic immersion and is not
asserted to be a global embedding. When $r=3N$, its local branches and the
genuine transitions between such charts are equal-dimensional local
canonical transformations by clauses 2-3 of that theorem. The drift, kick and velocity-Verlet maps of the mechanical splitting in exact
arithmetic are equal-dimensional local canonical transformations on their
admissible domains whenever those domains are nonempty, by
[[prop-cm-drift-kick-and-verlet-preserve-the-canonical-form]].

**(e) Status.** The item defines the canonical maps of the presentation and
fixes the dimension-aware pullback test of clause (a) and the equal-dimensional
matrix test of clause (b). It asserts no existence of a canonical map beyond
the listed suppliers, no global statement on multiply connected phase domains
and no empirical content; in particular, canonicity is a local condition on
the two-form, and an equal-dimensional canonical transformation need not admit
a globally defined real generating function, as the scope remark of this page
records.
items.physical_scope: The dimension-aware canonical-map datum of a declared potential presentation: $C^{1}$ maps, possibly between phase domains of different dimensions, that pull the target two-form back to the source two-form; their symplectic-immersion property; and, for equal-dimensional local canonical transformations, the square matrix, determinant and Hamiltonian-field transport consequences. The item records which model chart maps are canonical immersions and which are genuine full-dimensional transformations; it asserts no existence beyond its listed suppliers and no measured value.

items.title: The Hamiltonian evolution of a potential presentation preserves the two-form, the bracket and the determinant on its actual time-slice domains, also when the Hamiltonian depends on time
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]], the canonical maps of
[[def-cm13-canonical-map]] and the Hamiltonian field of
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]]: the Cartesian Hamiltonian
$H(t,x,p)=\tfrac12p\cdot\mathsf M^{-1}p+U(t,x)$ of class $C^{2}$ on
$I_{0}\times W$, where the potential $U$ and the residual forces $d$ are
those of [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and the data are those of
[[def-cm01-configuration]], [[def-cm01-units]]
([[def-cm12-hamiltonian]], [[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]]). Let
$t_{0}\in I_{0}$ and $z_{0}\in W$. Then there are reals $h>0$, $\rho>0$ and
an open neighbourhood $U_{0}\subseteq W$ of $z_{0}$ such that:

1. **(solution map)** the solutions $t\mapsto\Phi(t;y)$ of the Hamiltonian
   system $\dot z(t)=X_{H_{t}}(z(t))$ through $y\in U_{0}$ at time $t_{0}$
   are defined for $t\in[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]$, and the solution map
   $\Phi:[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]\times U_{0}\to W$ is $C^{1}$ in $y$; for each
   fixed $t$ the time-$t$ map $\Phi_{t}:=\Phi(t;\cdot)$ is a canonical map
   of the presentation between equal-dimensional phase domains, and thus a
   local canonical transformation on $U_{0}$:

$$D\Phi_{t}(y)^{\mathsf T}J\,D\Phi_{t}(y)=J,\qquad \Phi_{t}^{*}\omega=\omega\qquad(y\in U_{0}),$$

   and $\det D\Phi_{t}(y)=1$ for every $y\in U_{0}$.
2. **(bracket preservation)** For every $t\in[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]$ and all
   $C^{2}$ phase functions $f,g$ on $W$,
   $\{f\circ\Phi_{t},\,g\circ\Phi_{t}\}=\{f,g\}\circ\Phi_{t}$ on $U_{0}$;
   the brackets on the left are the pointwise coordinate brackets of the
   $C^{1}$ compositions defined in [[def-cm13-poisson]].
3. **(potential branch)** On the potential branch ($d\equiv0$) the curves
   $t\mapsto\Phi(t;y)$ are, through
   [[pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations]], the
   momentum-phase curves of the model's motions, so the model's Hamiltonian
   evolution preserves the presentation's two-form, bracket and determinant
   on the actual time-slice domains; the assertion is local in time, and no
   completeness of the flow is claimed.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation and the cited mathematics. It requires no autonomy of $H$: the
conclusion holds for each fixed pair of times on which the solutions exist.
items.physical_scope: Preservation of the symplectic structure by the model's Hamiltonian evolution: on the actual time-slice domains of a $C^{2}$ branch Hamiltonian, also for a time-dependent Hamiltonian, the equal-dimensional solution maps are local canonical transformations, preserve the bracket of $C^{2}$ phase functions (with the resulting $C^1$ compositions read through the defined pointwise bracket extension) and have unit determinant; hence the model's potential-branch flow preserves the presentation's two-form locally in time. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; no completeness, all-time assertion or measured value is claimed.

items.title: Equal-dimensional canonical transformations of a potential presentation conjugate Hamiltonian fields and transport systems and brackets
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]], the Hamiltonian fields of
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]], the bracket of [[def-cm13-poisson]] and the
canonical maps of [[def-cm13-canonical-map]]
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-configuration]],
[[def-cm01-units]]). Let $W_1,W_2$ be nonempty open subsets of phase domains
of the same dimension $2n$, and let $C:W_{1}\to W_{2}$ be a $C^{2}$ local
diffeomorphism with $C^*\omega_2=\omega_1$, hence an equal-dimensional local
canonical transformation in the sense of [[def-cm13-canonical-map]]. Let
$H:I_{0}\times W_{2}\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{2}$; write
$H\circ C$ for the function $(t,z)\mapsto H(t,C(z))$ on $I_{0}\times W_{1}$.
Then:

1. **(field transport)** For every $C^{2}$ function $f$ on $W_{2}$ and every
   $z\in W_{1}$,

$$DC(z)\,X_{f\circ C}(z)=X_{f}\bigl(C(z)\bigr),$$

   i.e. $C$ conjugates the Hamiltonian field of $f\circ C$ on $W_{1}$ to the
   field of $f$ on $W_{2}$.
2. **(bracket invariance)** For all $C^{2}$ functions $f,g$ on $W_{2}$,

$$\{f\circ C,\,g\circ C\}=\{f,g\}\circ C\qquad\text{on }W_{1},$$

   so the bracket of the presentation is invariant under canonical maps.
3. **(transport of solutions)** Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be a nonempty open
   interval and let $z:J\to W_{1}$ be a $C^{1}$ curve. Then $z$ solves
   $\dot z(t)=X_{(H\circ C)_{t}}(z(t))$ if and only if $t\mapsto C(z(t))$ solves
   $\dot w(t)=X_{H_{t}}(w(t))$ on $J$: the canonical map carries the
   Hamiltonian system of $H\circ C$ to that of $H$, with time dependence
   allowed.
4. **(instances)** Genuine transitions between full-dimensional ($r=3N$)
   charts of the presentation and the maps generated by first- and
   second-kind generating functions satisfy these transport conclusions.
   A fixed time-slice map $\Phi_{t_*}$ of
   [[pthm-cm13-flow-preservation]] is an additional instance for clauses 1-2
   when it has $C^2$ regularity, with $\Phi_{t_*}$ held fixed as the
   coordinate map. The flow-preservation theorem under its stated $C^2$
   Hamiltonian hypothesis guarantees only $C^1$ regularity; this item makes
   no field-transport claim for a slice known only to be $C^1$, and does not
   treat the moving family $t\mapsto\Phi_t$ as a single time-dependent
   coordinate transformation.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no empirical content and
no global existence of canonical maps.
items.physical_scope: Transformation theory for equal-dimensional local canonical transformations of the declared potential presentation: a $C^{2}$ local diffeomorphism preserving the two-form conjugates the Hamiltonian field of a phase function to the field of the composed function, preserves the model's Poisson bracket under composition, and carries solutions of one Hamiltonian system to solutions of the other, also for time-dependent Hamiltonians. No such ambient field-transport result is asserted for a lower-dimensional symplectic immersion. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no empirical content or global existence.

G. J. Sussman and J. Wisdom, Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics, second edition (MIT Press, 2014/2015), Sections 5.2-5.3: canonical transformations as maps between Hamiltonian systems preserving the dynamics, and the invariance of the Poisson bracket

D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Section 15.3: canonical transformations and the transformation of the Hamiltonian under a generating-function change of variables

items.title: A curve solves Hamilton's equations if and only if its velocity annihilates $d(p\cdot dq-H\,dt)$, with the three coordinate components computed
items.statement:
Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let
$W\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ be open and nonempty with coordinates
$z=(q,p)=(q^{1},\dots,q^{n},p_{1},\dots,p_{n})$, and let
$H:J\times W\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{1}$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]],
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). On $J\times W$ let
$\alpha:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}p_i\,dq^i-H\,dt$, a coordinate one-form with $C^1$
coefficients. Define its coordinate exterior derivative by
$d\alpha:=\sum_{a<b}(\partial_a\alpha_b-\partial_b\alpha_a)\,dy^a\wedge dy^b$
in the ordered coordinates $y=(t,q^1,\dots,q^n,p_1,\dots,p_n)$; this is a
continuous coordinate two-form, using the same alternating multilinear
convention as [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]] but making no smooth-form
claim. In expanded form, set

$$\sigma:=d\alpha=\sum_{i=1}^{n}dp_i\wedge dq^i+\sum_{i=1}^{n}H_{q^i}\,dt\wedge dq^i+\sum_{i=1}^{n}H_{p_i}\,dt\wedge dp_i.$$

Every coefficient of $\sigma$ is continuous because $H$ is $C^1$. Let
$J'\subseteq J$ be a nonempty open interval and let $z:J'\to W$ be a $C^{1}$
curve. Then the following are equivalent:

1. $z$ satisfies Hamilton's equations on $J'$:
   $\dot q^{i}(t)=H_{p_{i}}\bigl(t,z(t)\bigr)$ and
   $\dot p_{i}(t)=-H_{q^{i}}\bigl(t,z(t)\bigr)$ for $i=1,\dots,n$ and every
   $t\in J'$;
2. for every $t\in J'$ the covector
   $\iota_{(1,\dot z(t))}\sigma$ vanishes, that is
   $\sigma_{(t,z(t))}\bigl((1,\dot z(t)),w\bigr)=0$ for every
   $w\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{2n}$.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 4.1.5, printed pages 87-88 (PDF pages 93-94): the phase-space action $\int(p_i\dot q_i-H)\,dt$ with independent variations of $q_i$ and $p_i$, whose vanishing gives Hamilton's equations

D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Sections 15.1-15.2: Hamilton's equations in phase space and the differential of the phase-space action integrand

items.title: Liouville's theorem for a potential presentation: the phase-volume form $\omega^{3N}/(3N)!$ and the Lebesgue measure in each canonical chart are preserved by the Hamiltonian evolution on its actual domains
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), where the change-of-variables theorem below
requires it. Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and
mechanical Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the momentum charts and
two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the canonical coordinates of
[[def-cm13-canonical-form]], the canonical maps of
[[def-cm13-canonical-map]] and the flow of [[pthm-cm13-flow-preservation]]:
$H:I_{0}\times W\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$ with
$H(t,x,p)=\tfrac12p\cdot\mathsf M^{-1}p+U(t,x)$ on the Cartesian phase domain
$W=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ ([[def-cm12-hamiltonian]],
[[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]],
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-configuration]],
[[def-cm01-units]]). Write $n:=3N$ and let

$$\Omega:=\frac{1}{n!}\,\omega^{\wedge n}$$

be the **phase-volume form of the presentation**. Its dimension is
$[\Omega]=[\omega]^n=(\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1})^{3N}$, namely action to the
power $3N$; the Lebesgue measure $\lambda_{6N}$ in a canonical phase chart
has the same phase-volume unit. By
[[cor-symplectic-manifolds-have-a-canonical-orientation-and-volume-form]]
applied to the symplectic phase domain of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]], $\Omega$ is a nowhere-zero top form
on the $6N$-dimensional Cartesian phase domain. Pointwise compatibility of
pullback with wedge products shows that it is preserved by every
equal-dimensional canonical transformation, not by a lower-dimensional
symplectic immersion. Let $t_{0}\in I_{0}$, $z_{0}\in
W$ and let $\Phi_{t}=\Phi(t;\cdot)$ be the time-$t$ solution map of the
Hamiltonian system on the neighbourhood $U_{0}$ supplied by
[[pthm-cm13-flow-preservation]], with image
$V_{t}:=\Phi_{t}(U_{0})$. Then:

1. **(form preservation)** For every $t$ on the existence interval,
   $\Phi_{t}^{*}\Omega=\Omega$ on $U_{0}$; the time slices of the model's
   Hamiltonian evolution preserve the phase-volume form.
2. **(measure preservation)** For every $t$ on the existence interval and
   every bounded Borel set $A\subseteq U_{0}$ with
   $\overline A\subseteq U_{0}$, the sets $A$ and $\Phi_{t}(A)$ are
   Lebesgue measurable and

$$\lambda_{6N}\bigl(\Phi_{t}(A)\bigr)=\lambda_{6N}(A),$$

   where $\lambda_{6N}$ is the Lebesgue measure of the chart
   ([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]],
   [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]],
   [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]).
3. **(chart independence)** The measure statement is independent of the
   full-dimensional canonical chart: for two genuine $6N$-dimensional phase
   charts with a $C^{1}$ diffeomorphism transition $\Theta$ on an open
   overlap and a Borel set $B$ of finite measure in its domain,
   $\lambda_{6N}(\Theta(B))=\lambda_{6N}(B)$ because this
   equal-dimensional canonical transformation has $|\det D\Theta|=1$
   ([[def-cm13-canonical-form]],
   [[prop-cm-canonical-map-tests-and-hamiltonian-transport]]).
4. **(potential branch)** On the potential branch ($d\equiv0$) the time
   slices are the momentum-phase maps of the model's motions
   ([[pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations]]), so the
   model's Hamiltonian evolution conserves phase volume on its actual
   domains; no completeness and no all-time statement is claimed.
items.physical_scope: Phase-volume conservation for the declared potential presentation: the top form $\omega^{3N}/(3N)!$ is nowhere zero and is preserved by every time slice of the $C^{2}$ branch Hamiltonian evolution; the induced Lebesgue measure is preserved on bounded Borel sets of the actual flow domain, and measure comparison between charts is asserted only for genuine equal-dimensional chart transitions. The phase-volume unit is action to the power $3N$. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics, and in its measure-theoretic part it uses the Axiom of Countable Choice exactly where the cited change-of-variables theorem requires it; no empirical content is asserted.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 4.2, printed pages 88-90 (PDF pages 94-96): the proof that the phase-space volume in a neighbourhood is preserved, that the volume remains constant for all time, and the remark that the statement holds whether or not the system conserves energy

G. J. Sussman and J. Wisdom, Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics, second edition (MIT Press, 2014/2015), Section 5.3: Liouville's theorem as the statement that time evolution preserves phase-space volume, with canonical transformations also preserving phase volumes

D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Sections 15.1-15.2: the incompressibility of the Hamiltonian flow in phase space

items.title: Generating functions for a potential presentation: first- and second-kind data generate canonical maps locally, the local converse under an invertible projection, and the time-dependent Hamiltonian $K=H+\partial_tS$
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]], the Hamiltonian fields of
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]], the canonical maps of
[[def-cm13-canonical-map]] and the branch Hamiltonian $H$ of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]] and [[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]]
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-configuration]],
[[def-cm01-units]]). Write $n':=3N$ and let $O_{q},O_{Q},O_{P}\subseteq
Q$-coordinates and $\mathbb R^{n'}$ be as below. Then:

1. **(first kind)** Let $S:O_{q}\times O_{Q}\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{3}$
   with $\det S_{qQ}(q,Q)\neq0$ everywhere
   ([[def-cm-generating-function-of-the-first-and-second-kind]]), and define
   the **local map generated by $S$** by solving $p=S_{q}(q,Q)$ for
   $Q=Q(q,p)$ and setting $P:=-S_{Q}(q,Q)$: a $C^{2}$ map
   $C:(q,p)\mapsto(Q,P)$ defined on a neighbourhood of each point of the
   solution set. Then $C$ is a canonical $C^{2}$ local diffeomorphism of the
   presentation: $DC^{\mathsf T}J\,DC=J$, $C^{*}\omega=\omega$ and
   $|\det DC|=1$; and the one-form identity $p\cdot dq-P\cdot dQ=dS$ holds on
   the $(q,Q)$-domain ([[prop-cm-generating-functions-yield-canonical-maps]]).
2. **(second kind)** Let $S:O_{q}\times O_{P}\to\mathbb R$ be $C^{3}$ with
   $\det S_{qP}\neq0$ everywhere, and define the local map by
   $p=S_{q}(q,P)$, $Q=S_{P}(q,P)$. Then it is again a canonical $C^{2}$ local
   diffeomorphism of the presentation with the recorded identity
   $p\cdot dq+Q\cdot dP=dS$.
3. **(local converse)** Let $C$ be a $C^{2}$ canonical diffeomorphism between
   nonempty open subsets of the presentation's Cartesian phase domains, and
   suppose that the projection $z\mapsto(q(z),Q(z))$ onto the old position
   and the new position has invertible derivative at a point $z_{0}$. Then
   there are a neighbourhood of $z_{0}$ and a $C^{3}$ function
   $S:O_{q}\times O_{Q}\to\mathbb R$ with $\det S_{qQ}\neq0$ whose generated
   map agrees with $C$ on that neighbourhood
   ([[prop-cm-canonical-map-locally-has-a-generating-function]]).
4. **(time-dependent generating function)** Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be a
   nonempty open interval and let $S:J\times O_{q}\times O_{Q}\to\mathbb R$
   be of class $C^{3}$ with $\det S_{qQ}(t,q,Q)\neq0$ everywhere; for each
   $t$ let $C_{t}$ be the first-kind map generated by $S_{t}$. Assume the
   values $(q,p)$ used below lie in the domain of $H$ of
   [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]], and set
   $p:=S_{q}(t,q,Q)$, $P:=-S_{Q}(t,q,Q)$ and
   $K(t,q,Q):=H\bigl(t,q,S_{q}(t,q,Q)\bigr)+\partial_tS(t,q,Q)$. The
   functions $S$ in clauses 1-4 have action dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1}$;
   in clause 4, $\partial_tS$ has energy dimension
   $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}$, so the sum defining $K$ is dimensionally
   consistent. Then:
   (a) each $C_{t}$ is a canonical $C^{2}$ local diffeomorphism of the
   presentation; (b) the Poincare-Cartan identity

$$p\cdot dq-H\,dt=P\cdot dQ-K\,dt+dS$$

   holds on $J\times O_{q}\times O_{Q}$
   ([[prop-cm-time-dependent-generating-function]]); and (c) writing $K$ as
   a function of $(t,Q,P)$ through the correspondence
   $(t,q,Q)\leftrightarrow(t,Q,P)$, a $C^{1}$ curve $t\mapsto(q(t),p(t))$
   satisfies $q'=H_{p}$, $p'=-H_{q}$ if and only if
   $t\mapsto(Q(t),P(t))=C_{t}(q(t),p(t))$ satisfies $Q'=K_{P}$,
   $P'=-K_{Q}$ on the interval where both descriptions are defined.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no global generating
function, no existence of a canonical map with prescribed data beyond the
local statements, and no empirical content.
items.physical_scope: Generating-function theory for the declared potential presentation: first- and second-kind generating functions of action dimension generate equal-dimensional canonical local diffeomorphisms with the recorded one-form identities and unit determinant; a canonical diffeomorphism with invertible $(q,Q)$-projection is locally generated in the first kind; and for a time-dependent generating function the time derivative has energy dimension and the transformed Hamiltonian is $K=H+\partial_tS$, with the Hamilton systems of $H$ and $K$ carried into one another by the generated time-dependent map. The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no global generating function and no empirical content.

items.title: Fundamental brackets and Bracket evolution on explicit one-label data: $\{x^a,H\}=p_a/m$, $\{p_a,H\}=-U_{x^a}$, and the oscillator check
items.statement:
Declare the one-label model of the force branch
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window
$I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$, a $C^{2}$ potential
$U:\mathbb R\times Q\to\mathbb R$ and no residual forces
([[def-cm01-configuration]], [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]). By
[[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]] the presentation is hyperregular on
the Cartesian chart with $H(t,x,p)=\tfrac12m^{-1}\lvert p\rvert^{2}+U(t,x)$
([[def-cm12-hamiltonian]]), the two-form is
$\omega=\sum_{a=1}^{3}dx^{a}\wedge dp_{a}$
([[def-cm13-two-form]], [[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]]) and the bracket
is [[def-cm13-poisson]]. Then:

1. the canonical coordinates satisfy the **fundamental brackets**
   $\{x^{a},x^{b}\}=0$, $\{p_{a},p_{b}\}=0$ and
   $\{x^{a},p_{b}\}=\delta^{a}_{b}$ for all $a,b\in\{1,2,3\}$
   ([[pthm-cm13-bracket-identities]] clause 5);
2. the brackets of the coordinates with the Hamiltonian recover the model's
   velocities and forces:
   $\{x^{a},H\}=H_{p_{a}}=m^{-1}p_{a}$ and
   $\{p_{a},H\}=-H_{x^{a}}=-U_{x^{a}}(t,x)$; hence Hamilton's equations read
   $\dot x^{a}=\{x^{a},H\}$, $\dot p_{a}=\{p_{a},H\}$
   ([[pthm-cm13-bracket-identities]] clause 4,
   [[pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations]] clause 1);
3. along every solution of the Hamiltonian system and for every $C^{1}$ phase
   function $f$, $\frac{d}{dt}f(t,x(t),p(t))=\partial_{t}f+\{f,H\}$
   ([[pthm-cm13-observable-evolution]] clause 1);
4. on the **isotropic oscillator instance** $U(x)=\tfrac12k\lvert x\rvert^{2}$
   with $k>0$, one has $\{p_{a},H\}=-kx^{a}$ and $\{H,H\}=0$, and every
   solution of the Hamiltonian system has constant
   $H=\tfrac12m^{-1}\lvert p\rvert^{2}+\tfrac12k\lvert x\rvert^{2}$ on its
   domain, the Hamiltonian form of the model's energy conservation
   ([[pthm-cm13-observable-evolution]] clause 2,
   [[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]]).

All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement
is reported.
items.physical_scope: A worked computation of the bracket of a declared one-label potential presentation: the fundamental brackets of the canonical coordinates, the bracket of the coordinates with the branch Hamiltonian reproducing velocity and force, and the evolution identity and energy constancy on the isotropic oscillator instance. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement is reported.

items.title: The isotropic oscillator of the model: explicit solution, the determinant and matrix tests on each two-dimensional block, and the area and energy checks
items.statement:
Declare the one-label model of the force branch
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window
$\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$, the time-independent
potential $U(x)=\tfrac12k\lvert x\rvert^{2}$ with $k>0$ and no residual forces
([[def-cm01-configuration]], [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]); this is the **isotropic
oscillator instance**. By [[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]] the branch
Hamiltonian is

$$H(x,p)=\frac{\lvert p\rvert^{2}}{2m}+\frac{k\lvert x\rvert^{2}}{2},\qquad \omega_{0}:=\sqrt{k/m}>0,$$

The stiffness and angular frequency have dimensions $[k]=\mu\tau^{-2}$ and
$[\omega_0]=\tau^{-1}$. The grouped phase coordinates are
$z=(x^1,x^2,x^3,p_1,p_2,p_3)$, with $[x^a]=\ell$ and
$[p_a]=\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; hence the six-dimensional phase-volume unit is
$[\omega^{\wedge3}/3!]=(\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1})^3$, action cubed.

on the Cartesian phase domain $\mathbb R^{6}$, with the two-form
$\omega=\sum_{a=1}^{3}dx^{a}\wedge dp_{a}$
([[def-cm13-two-form]], [[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]]) and the
Hamiltonian field $X_{H}=(\mathsf M^{-1}p,-\nabla_{x}U)$
([[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]], [[pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations]]).
Then:

1. for every initial datum $(x,p)$ the curve

$$x^{a}(t)=x^{a}\cos(\omega_{0}t)+\frac{p_{a}}{m\omega_{0}}\sin(\omega_{0}t),\qquad p_{a}(t)=-m\omega_{0}x^{a}\sin(\omega_{0}t)+p_{a}\cos(\omega_{0}t)\qquad(a=1,2,3)$$

   solves the Hamiltonian system for all $t\in\mathbb R$;
2. in the grouped order $z=(x,p)$ its derivative is
   $$D\Phi_t=\begin{pmatrix}cI_3&(m\omega_0)^{-1}sI_3\\-m\omega_0sI_3&cI_3\end{pmatrix},\qquad c=\cos(\omega_0t),\quad s=\sin(\omega_0t),$$
   and for $J_{\mathrm{gr}}=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_3\\-I_3&0\end{pmatrix}$
   direct block multiplication gives $D\Phi_t^{\mathsf T}J_{\mathrm{gr}}D\Phi_t=J_{\mathrm{gr}}$ because $c^2+s^2=1$. If
   $T(x^1,x^2,x^3,p_1,p_2,p_3)=(x^1,p_1,x^2,p_2,x^3,p_3)$ is the
   permutation to interleaved order, then $TD\Phi_tT^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(A,A,A)$ and $TJ_{\mathrm{gr}}T^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(J_2,J_2,J_2)$, where
   $A=\begin{pmatrix}c&(m\omega_0)^{-1}s\\-m\omega_0s&c\end{pmatrix}$;
   each block satisfies $A^{\mathsf T}J_2A=J_2$ and $\det A=1$.
   Therefore $\det D\Phi_t=(\det A)^3=1$, so the time-$t$ map is canonical
   ([[pthm-cm13-flow-preservation]],
   [[prop-cm-canonical-map-tests-and-hamiltonian-transport]]);
3. explicit volume check in the numeric coordinates measured in the declared
   SI units: the image of the unit square
   $[0,1]^{2}\subseteq\{(x^{1},p_{1})\}$ under $A$ is the parallelogram with
   area $\lvert\det A\rvert=1$, and the image of the box
   $[0,1]^{3}\times[0,1]^{3}$ has numeric six-volume
   $|\det D\Phi_t|=1$, corresponding to physical phase-volume dimension
   action cubed;
4. the energy is constant along the flow,
   $H(x(t),p(t))=H(x,p)$, and $\{H,H\}=0$
   ([[pthm-cm13-observable-evolution]] clause 2).

All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement
is reported.

items.title: The free particle of the model: the flow $Q=q+(t/m)p$ generated by the first-kind function $S_t(q,Q)=-m\lvert Q-q\rvert^{2}/(2t)$, the projection check and the exact change of $\lambda$
items.statement:
Declare the one-label model of the force branch
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window
$\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$, zero potential $U\equiv0$
and no residual forces (the **free particle instance**,
[[def-cm01-configuration]], [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]). By
[[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]] the branch Hamiltonian is
$H(x,p)=\lvert p\rvert^{2}/(2m)$ with Hamiltonian system
$\dot x=m^{-1}p$, $\dot p=0$
([[def-cm12-hamiltonian]], [[pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations]]).
Then:

1. for every initial datum the maximal solution is

$$\Phi_{t}(x,p)=\bigl(x+(t/m)\,p,\ p\bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$

   the free-particle flow of the presentation;
2. for $t\neq0$ the function
   $S_{t}(q,Q):=-\frac{m}{2t}\lvert Q-q\rvert^{2}$ is of class $C^{\infty}$
   on $\mathbb R^{3}\times\mathbb R^{3}$ with
   $[S_t]=[m][Q-q]^2/[t]=\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1}$ (action),
   $S_{t,qQ}=(m/t)I_{3}$ invertible everywhere, and the first-kind map it
   generates is exactly $\Phi_{t}$: indeed
   $p=S_{t,q}=m(Q-q)/t$ gives $Q=q+(t/m)p$, and
   $P=-S_{t,Q}=m(Q-q)/t=p$; consequently $\Phi_{t}$ is a canonical map of
   the presentation with $\lvert\det D\Phi_{t}\rvert=1$
   ([[pthm-cm13-generating-functions]] clauses 1,
   [[def-cm-generating-function-of-the-first-and-second-kind]],
   [[prop-cm-generating-functions-yield-canonical-maps]]);
3. projection check: the map
   $(q,p)\mapsto(q,Q)=(q,q+(t/m)p)$ has invertible derivative
   $\begin{pmatrix}I_{3}&0\\ I_{3}&(t/m)I_{3}\end{pmatrix}$ for $t\neq0$,
   while the family degenerates at $t=0$: $S_{t}$ has no value there and the
   projection becomes singular, so this family does not represent the
   identity map;
4. the canonical one-form changes by an exact form along the flow:
   $\Phi_{t}^{*}\lambda=\lambda+t\,dK$ with $K=\lvert p\rvert^{2}/(2m)$,
   because $\Phi_{t}^{*}\lambda=P\cdot dQ=p\cdot\bigl(dq+(t/m)dp\bigr)=\lambda+(t/m)\,d\bigl(\lvert p\rvert^{2}/2\bigr)$;
   in particular $\Phi_{t}^{*}d\lambda=d\lambda$, recovering canonicity
   directly ([[def-cm13-two-form]],
   [[prop-cm-canonical-map-tests-and-hamiltonian-transport]]).

All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement
is reported.

items.statement:
Declare the one-label model of the force branch
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$, configuration
domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$, a $C^{2}$ potential and no residual forces, and let
$X:\Omega\to Q$ be a generalized-coordinate **chart** of the configuration
domain: $r=3$, $X$ of class $C^{3}$, $DX(q)$ invertible for every
$q\in\Omega$ ([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm01-configuration]], [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]). Let the generalized
coordinates have declared dimensions $[q^a]=\gamma_a$; their conjugate
generalized momenta $\pi_a=\partial\widetilde L/\partial\dot q^a$ have
dimensions $[\pi_a]=\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1}\gamma_a^{-1}$. The Cartesian
positions $X^i(q)$ have dimension $\ell$ and their conjugate Cartesian
momenta $P_i$ have dimension $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$, by
[[def-cm01-units]] and [[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]].
The induced momentum chart transition of the presentation is

$$\Phi_{X}(q,\pi)=\bigl(X(q),\ \mathsf M\,DX(q)G(q)^{-1}\pi\bigr)=\bigl(X(q),\ DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}\pi\bigr),$$

the second equality because
$\mathsf M\,DX\,G^{-1}=DX^{-\mathsf T}$ when $DX$ is invertible and
$G=DX^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX$
([[def-cm13-two-form]], [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]],
[[def-cm12-hyperregularity]]). Then:

1. the function
   $S(q,P):=P\cdot X(q)=\sum_{i=1}^{3}P_iX^i(q)$ on
   $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{3}$ is of class $C^{3}$ and has action dimension
   $[S]=[P_i][X^i]=\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1}$; its mixed derivative matrix
   $S_{qP}$ is $DX(q)^{\mathsf T}$, whose determinant is nonzero. Here $P$
   is the new Cartesian momentum, while $\pi$ is the old generalized
   momentum. The second-kind relations are
   $\pi=S_q=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}P$ and $Q=S_P=X(q)$, so solving for $P$ gives
   $(q,\pi)\mapsto(X(q),DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}\pi)$, exactly $\Phi_X$;
   consequently $\Phi_X$ is a canonical map of the presentation with
   $|\det D\Phi_X|=1$
   ([[pthm-cm13-generating-functions]] clause 2,
   [[def-cm-generating-function-of-the-first-and-second-kind]],
   [[prop-cm-generating-functions-yield-canonical-maps]]);
2. determinant check: with the block decomposition in source coordinates
   $(q,\pi)$ and target coordinates $(Q,P)$ the derivative is block
   triangular,

$$D\Phi_{X}=\begin{pmatrix}DX(q)&0\\ \partial_{q}\bigl(DX^{-\mathsf T}\pi\bigr)&DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}\end{pmatrix},\qquad \det D\Phi_X=\det DX(q)\cdot\det DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}=1;$$

3. the $(q,Q)$-projection $(q,\pi)\mapsto(q,X(q))$ is independent of the
   momentum and has derivative $\begin{pmatrix}I_{3}&0\\ DX(q)&0\end{pmatrix}$
   of rank $3<6$ at every point: it is nowhere invertible. Since a first-kind
   generating function requires the relation $p=S_{q}(q,Q)$ to be solvable
   for $Q$, i.e. the map $(q,Q)\mapsto(q,S_{q}(q,Q))$ to be a local
   diffeomorphism, the transition $\Phi_{X}$ admits **no first-kind
   generating function** near any point; the second-kind representation of
   claim 1 is the available local description
   ([[pthm-cm13-generating-functions]] clause 3,
   [[prop-cm-canonical-map-locally-has-a-generating-function]]);
4. contrast — the Cartesian momentum shift: for a constant $c\in\mathbb R^{3}$
   of momentum dimension the map
   $C(q,p)=(q,p+c)$ of the Cartesian chart is canonical trivially
   ($DC=I_{6}$), its first-kind projection is degenerate identically, and it
   has the **global** second-kind generating function
   $S(q,P)=q\cdot(P-c)$, also of action dimension, since $S_q=P-c$ and
   $S_P=q$.

All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement
is reported.
items.physical_scope: A worked projection and generating-function computation for the declared potential presentation: a genuine chart $X$ of the configuration domain induces the momentum chart transition from generalized momentum $\pi$ to Cartesian momentum $P$, $(q,\pi)\mapsto(X(q),DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}\pi)$, generated in the second kind by the action-dimensioned function $S(q,P)=P\cdot X(q)$; the transition has unit determinant and fails the first-kind projection hypothesis identically. The degenerate case is compared with the momentum shift, whose second-kind generating function is global. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement is reported.

items.title: Determinant tests on explicit linear maps: $\det A=1$ is equivalent to canonicity in dimension two, and strictly weaker in dimension four (the volume-preserving shear)
items.statement:
Let $J_{2}= egin{pmatrix}0&1\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and, in the ordered
coordinates $(q^{1},p_{1},q^{2},p_{2})$ of $\mathbb R^{4}$, let
$J_{4}=\operatorname{diag}(J_{2},J_{2})$ be the standard symplectic matrix of
the phase domain $\mathbb R^{4}$
([[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]]); recall that a
linear map $A$ is canonical exactly when $A^{\mathsf T}JA=J$
([[prop-cm-canonical-map-tests-and-hamiltonian-transport]]). Then:

1. **(dimension two)** For $A= egin{pmatrix}a&b\c&d\end{pmatrix}$ one has

$$A^{\mathsf T}J_{2}A=(ad-bc)\,J_{2}=(\det A)\,J_{2},$$

   so an invertible $A$ is canonical if and only if $\det A=1$: in one degree
   of freedom canonicity and oriented area preservation coincide. For instance
   $A= egin{pmatrix}2&1\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ has $\det A=1$ and is canonical.
2. **(scaling)** For $\lambda
eq0$ the block-diagonal map
   $C(q,p)=(\lambda q,\lambda^{-1}p)$ on the phase domain
   $\mathbb R^{2n}$ is canonical: its derivative
   $\operatorname{diag}(\lambda I_{n},\lambda^{-1}I_{n})$ satisfies
   $DC^{\mathsf T}J\,DC=J$ and $\det DC=1$; it even preserves the canonical
   one-form, $C^{*}\lambda=\lambda$, because
   $(\lambda^{-1}p)\cdot d(\lambda q)=p\cdot dq$.
3. **(volume preservation is weaker in dimension four)** The linear shear

$$C(q^{1},q^{2},p_{1},p_{2})=(q^{1},\,q^{2}+q^{1},\,p_{1},\,p_{2})$$

   is written in grouped coordinates $(q^1,q^2,p_1,p_2)$, whose
   symplectic matrix is $J_{\mathrm{grp}}= egin{pmatrix}0&I_2\-I_2&0\end{pmatrix}$.
   It has $\det DC=1$, so it preserves volume, but
   $DC^{\mathsf T}J_{\mathrm{grp}}\,DC=J_{\mathrm{grp}}+e_{1}e_{4}^{\mathsf T}-e_{4}e_{1}^{\mathsf T}
eq J_{\mathrm{grp}}$:
   the $(1,4)$-entry is $1$ instead of $0$. Equivalently the fundamental
   bracket $\{Q^{2},P_{1}\}=1$ does not vanish, while canonicity would force
   $\{Q^{2},P_{1}\}=\delta^{2}_{1}=0$. Hence $|\det DC|=1$ does **not**
   imply canonicity in dimension $4$.
4. **(positive control)** If $A=\operatorname{diag}(A_{1},A_{2})$ in the
   ordered coordinates $(q^{1},p_{1},q^{2},p_{2})$ with each $2	imes2$ block
   satisfying $A_{i}^{\mathsf T}J_{2}A_{i}=J_{2}$, then
   $A^{\mathsf T}J_{4}A=J_{4}$: canonicity is preserved blockwise.
